key_insight: Photovoltaics look energy-efficient at the panel level, but their net energy falls sharply once reliable, around-the-clock supply constraints and firming are included.
engineering_relevance: For power-system design, the main challenge is not making PV alone efficient, but preserving sufficient net-energy surplus when storage, backup, and grid delivery are added.
method: Includes component turnover, grids, storage, renewable overbuild, dispatchable backup, and fuel supply
Compares unfirmed renewable supply with battery, hydrogen, and gas-firmed electricity
evidence_signal: The abstract reports EROI and lifecycle-emissions ranges for multiple firming pathways, showing strong declines in EROI and higher GWP100 as reliability requirements increase.
watch_item: This is an illustrative accounting benchmark, not a simulation or optimization of a real power system, so results should not be treated as deployment predictions.
paper_title: Photovoltaics beyond the panel: system-level net energy under grid and firming constraints
